five_minutes: GOI dated‑security auction of ₹33 trn likely lifts 10‑yr G‑sec yields, pressuring equity valuations.
RBI’s overnight Variable Rate Repo auction adds ₹50 bn liquidity, could temper short‑term rate spikes.
Gold price rebounds from a 14‑month low, reviving interest in sovereign gold bonds and hedges.
Nvidia’s $1 tn market‑cap gain after Jensen Huang’s return fuels AI‑related stock rally, supporting Indian IT exporters.
India‑EU free‑trade pact slated for Dec 16 promises duty‑free access for 93% of exports, bolstering export‑oriented sectors.

theses.thesis: Crypto is rising because markets expect a global recession (crypto trading as the recession hedge)
US policy decisions under Trump are pushing the US economy toward decline, contrary to the stated growth narrative
Gold and silver will NOT rise further even in a recession, because they are already at all-time highs

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: Nvidia adds ~$1 tn market cap after Jensen Huang’s return, lifting AI‑related equities worldwide
items.what_happened: Nvidia shares surged nearly $1 tn in market value following the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang, driving a 6.5% gain in the Nasdaq.
items.why_it_matters: The rally energises AI‑focused stocks, benefiting Indian IT exporters and semiconductor‑related companies that track global AI demand.

items.headline: AI trade resurgence lifts Taiwanese index 9%, reinforcing momentum in semiconductor and AI stocks
items.what_happened: Taiwan’s stock index rose 9% after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang, reviving investor appetite for AI‑related semiconductor exposure.
items.why_it_matters: Strong performance in Taiwan’s AI sector signals robust global demand, supporting export‑oriented Indian tech firms and influencing sector allocation.

items.headline: RBI to run a ₹50 bn overnight Variable Rate Repo auction on 25 Nov, offering short‑term liquidity
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank announced a Variable Rate Repo auction of ₹50 bn for one‑day tenor, to be conducted on 25 Nov.
items.why_it_matters: Injecting short‑term liquidity can curb spikes in overnight rates, supporting money‑market stability and influencing short‑term G‑sec yields.

items.headline: RBI re‑affirms D‑SIB list, adding CET1 buffer for SBI, HDFC and ICICI, tightening capital for top banks
items.what_happened: Reserve Bank of India released the 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks, keeping SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank as D‑SIBs with an extra CET1 requirement.
items.why_it_matters: Higher capital buffers raise funding costs for the three biggest banks, potentially affecting their earnings and weight in bank‑focused funds.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: FEMA amendment expands export‑import categories, easing compliance for exporters and may modestly support INR
items.what_happened: RBI issued the Second Amendment to the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, adding new categories and clarifying procedures.
items.why_it_matters: Simplified FX rules can reduce transaction frictions for exporters, supporting export flows and potentially tempering INR pressure from trade‑related outflows.

items.headline: Private investment project announcements jump 58.5% YoY to ₹26.6 lakh cr in H1 FY27, indicating a strengthening pipeline
items.what_happened: The Confederation of Indian Industry reported a 58.5% rise in announced private‑investment projects, totaling ₹26.6 lakh cr in the first half of FY27.
items.why_it_matters: Higher private‑sector investment signals confidence in growth, potentially boosting construction, infrastructure and related equities.

items.headline: RBI Governor’s meeting with NBFCs signals tighter credit monitoring, could constrain NBFC funding
items.what_happened: The RBI Governor met CEOs of selected NBFCs and housing finance companies in Mumbai on 23 Nov to discuss sector health and regulatory expectations.
items.why_it_matters: Heightened supervisory focus may lead to stricter loan‑to‑value norms or liquidity caps, affecting NBFC funding costs and credit supply to SMEs and housing.

items.headline: India‑Canada trade pact near finalisation, likely to open new market avenues for exporters
items.what_happened: Officials said India and Canada are ‘very close’ to concluding negotiations on a comprehensive trade agreement, after the sixth round of talks.
items.why_it_matters: The pact could reduce tariffs and non‑tariff barriers, benefitting sectors such as agri‑food, IT services and renewable energy, and may improve the trade balance.

items.headline: India‑EU free‑trade agreement expected to sign Dec 16, granting duty‑free access for 93% of Indian exports
items.what_happened: German state leader announced that negotiations for the India‑EU FTA concluded in January and the signing is slated for 16 December.
items.why_it_matters: Duty‑free access will lower costs for Indian exporters in sectors like textiles, pharmaceuticals and IT services, supporting export‑linked earnings and potentially strengthening the rupee.

items.headline: GOI dated‑security auction of ₹33 trn adds supply, likely nudging 10‑yr G‑sec yields higher
items.what_happened: Government of India announced re‑issue of four dated securities totaling ₹33 trn, with the first tranche (₹9 trn 6.20% 2029) auctioned on 17 Nov.
items.why_it_matters: Higher bond supply can push yields up, lowering bond prices and raising equity discount rates; the added supply also influences RBI’s liquidity management.

items.headline: Gold price rebounds from 14‑month low, MCX gold at ₹1.26 lakh/10 gm, reviving interest in gold as a hedge
items.what_happened: The MCX gold rate closed at ₹1,26,021 per 10 gm on 24 Nov, while the international USD price sits around $3,635 per ounce, marking a bounce from a 14‑month trough.
items.why_it_matters: Higher gold prices improve the appeal of sovereign gold bonds and can draw capital into safe‑haven assets, influencing portfolio allocations across equities and fixed income.

items.headline: Premature redemption option for SGB 2021‑22 Series I may boost demand for sovereign gold bonds
items.what_happened: The government announced that premature redemption of the Sovereign Gold Bond 2021‑22 Series I is permissible after the fifth year, with redemption price set at the prevailing market price on the redemption date.
items.why_it_matters: Liquidity provision can make SGBs more attractive to investors seeking gold exposure, potentially supporting gold prices and offering a low‑cost hedge for portfolios.
